title: FlytWERX ACS Maneuver Standards Checker Data

acs.documentTitle: Instrument Rating – Airplane Airman Certification Standards

page.disclaimer: This checker summarizes selected FAA ACS performance standards for training and debrief use. Always use the current official FAA ACS and the applicable POH/AFM. FlytWERX data supports review and does not replace evaluator judgment or approved aircraft indications.

holding-procedures.name: Holding Procedures
holding-procedures.objective: Holding procedures solely by reference to instruments.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain the assigned or selected altitude within ACS tolerance.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the applicable or selected airspeed within ACS tolerance.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain selected headings within ACS tolerance.

metrics.label: Course Tracking
metrics.description: Track the selected course, radial, or bearing within three-quarter-scale CDI deflection.

criteria: Use an appropriate entry for the assigned standard, nonstandard, published, or non-published hold.
Reduce to the holding airspeed appropriate for altitude before reaching the fix.
Recognize the holding fix and promptly initiate the entry.
Comply with leg-length and other published or assigned restrictions.
Apply wind correction to maintain the desired holding pattern.
Comply with ATC reporting requirements and restrictions.

reviewVariables.label: AIRSPEED
reviewVariables.text: Review airspeed control before and during the hold.

reviewVariables.label: ALTITUDE
reviewVariables.text: Review altitude deviations through each circuit.

reviewVariables.label: WIND
reviewVariables.text: Review wind-correction changes and pattern shape.

reviewVariables.label: TRACK
reviewVariables.text: Review CDI/course tracking and fix crossings.

instrument-flight.name: Instrument Flight
instrument-flight.objective: Basic flight maneuvers solely by reference to instruments.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain altitude during level flight.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain selected headings.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain selected airspeed.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Maintain selected bank angles during turns.

criteria: Maintain altitude, heading, airspeed, and bank within the applicable ACS tolerances.
Use a continuous instrument cross-check.
Interpret instrument indications correctly.
Apply appropriate pitch, bank, power, and trim corrections.

reviewVariables.label: SCAN
reviewVariables.text: Review continuity and prioritization of the instrument scan.

source.documentTitle: Instrument Rating – Airplane Airman Certification Standards

unusual-attitude-recovery.name: Recovery from Unusual Flight Attitudes
unusual-attitude-recovery.objective: Recover from unusual flight attitudes solely by reference to instruments.

metrics.label: Recovery
metrics.description: Recognize the unusual attitude and apply the appropriate recovery procedure.

metrics.label: Aircraft Limits
metrics.description: Maintain control and remain within aircraft operating limitations.

criteria: Recognize the unusual attitude using available flight instruments.
Apply the appropriate recovery procedure without delay.
Use appropriate pitch, bank, power, and configuration inputs.
Avoid inappropriate control inputs caused by spatial disorientation.
Return to stabilized instrument flight while observing aircraft limitations.

reviewVariables.label: RECOGNITION
reviewVariables.text: Review how quickly the attitude was recognized.

reviewVariables.label: STABILIZATION
reviewVariables.text: Review transition back to stable instrument flight.

source.documentTitle: Instrument Rating – Airplane Airman Certification Standards

intercepting-tracking.name: Intercepting and Tracking Navigation Systems
intercepting-tracking.objective: Intercept and track courses, radials, bearings, and DME arcs using installed navigation systems.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain altitude while intercepting and tracking.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain airspeed while intercepting and tracking.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain selected headings as required by the task.

metrics.label: DME Arc
metrics.description: Maintain the specified DME arc distance when applicable.

criteria: Select, tune, identify, and verify the appropriate navigation source.
Determine aircraft position relative to the desired course, radial, bearing, or arc.
Select an appropriate intercept angle and establish the intercept.
Apply wind correction to maintain the desired track.
Maintain altitude, airspeed, and heading within task tolerances.
Monitor navigation displays and identify system or signal abnormalities.

reviewVariables.label: NAV SOURCE
reviewVariables.text: Confirm correct source selection and identification.

source.documentTitle: Instrument Rating – Airplane Airman Certification Standards
source.taskName: Intercepting and Tracking Navigational Systems and DME Arcs

departure-enroute-arrival.name: Departure, En Route, and Arrival Operations
departure-enroute-arrival.objective: Conduct published or assigned IFR departure, en route, and arrival procedures.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain the assigned or selected altitude within ACS tolerance.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the applicable or selected airspeed within ACS tolerance.

metrics.label: Heading
metrics.description: Maintain selected headings within ACS tolerance.

metrics.label: Procedure
metrics.description: Fly the applicable procedure, clearance, altitude, and navigation guidance.

criteria: Use current charts and navigation data.
Set up and verify navigation equipment before each phase.
Comply with ATC clearances and published procedure restrictions.
Maintain airspeed, altitude, and headings within ACS tolerances.
Apply appropriate wind correction and track the assigned route.
Use checklists and manage automation appropriately.

reviewVariables.label: CLEARANCE
reviewVariables.text: Review compliance with assigned routing and restrictions.

reviewVariables.label: AUTOMATION
reviewVariables.text: Review mode awareness and automation use.

source.documentTitle: Instrument Rating – Airplane Airman Certification Standards
source.taskName: Departure, En Route, and Arrival Operations

nonprecision-approach.name: Non-Precision Approach
nonprecision-approach.objective: Conduct a non-precision instrument approach to the applicable minimums.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain approach airspeed within tolerance.

metrics.label: Course
metrics.description: Maintain lateral guidance within three-quarter-scale CDI deflection.

metrics.label: MDA
metrics.description: Remain at or above MDA and within 100 feet above it, when applicable, through the VDP or MAP.

metrics.label: Pre-Final Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain assigned/published altitude prior to the final approach segment.

criteria: Complete the selected non-precision approach using current procedure information.
Set up and verify the required navigation equipment.
Comply with ATC clearances and checklist requirements.
Establish the appropriate configuration and a stabilized descent.
Maintain lateral guidance, airspeed, and MDA requirements within ACS tolerances.
At the MAP/VDP, continue only with required visual references or execute the missed approach.

precision-approach.name: Precision Approach
precision-approach.objective: Conduct a precision or approach with vertical guidance to the applicable decision altitude/height.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain approach airspeed within tolerance.

metrics.label: Lateral Guidance
metrics.description: Maintain lateral guidance within the ACS limit on final.

metrics.label: Vertical Guidance
metrics.description: Maintain vertical guidance within the ACS limit on final.

metrics.label: Pre-Final Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain required altitude prior to the final approach segment.

criteria: Complete the selected precision/vertical-guidance approach using current procedure information.
Set up, identify, and verify required navigation equipment.
Comply with ATC clearances and checklist requirements.
Establish a stabilized final approach with appropriate configuration.
Maintain lateral/vertical guidance and airspeed within ACS tolerances.
At decision altitude/height, continue only with required visual references or execute the missed approach.

missed-approach.name: Missed Approach
missed-approach.objective: Execute the published or assigned missed approach procedure.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the recommended missed-approach airspeed.

metrics.label: Heading / Course
metrics.description: Maintain heading, course, or bearing within tolerance.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain assigned or published altitude(s) within tolerance after level-off.

metrics.label: Climb
metrics.description: Establish the appropriate climb and configuration promptly.

criteria: Promptly initiate the missed approach when required.
Apply power, establish the appropriate pitch attitude, and configure for climb.
Navigate and comply with the published or assigned missed-approach procedure.
Maintain recommended airspeed, course/heading, and altitude within ACS tolerances.
Communicate with ATC as appropriate.
Complete applicable checklist items and manage workload.

reviewVariables.label: INITIATION
reviewVariables.text: Review delay between decision and missed-approach initiation.

reviewVariables.label: POWER
reviewVariables.text: Review power application and climb establishment.

reviewVariables.label: NAVIGATION
reviewVariables.text: Review compliance with the missed-approach path.

source.documentTitle: Instrument Rating – Airplane Airman Certification Standards

circling-approach.name: Circling Approach
circling-approach.objective: Transition from an instrument approach to a circling maneuver and position for landing.

metrics.label: Airspeed
metrics.description: Maintain the appropriate circling airspeed.

metrics.label: Altitude
metrics.description: Maintain circling altitude until a normal descent to landing is appropriate.

metrics.label: Heading / Track
metrics.description: Maintain desired heading or track within tolerance where applicable.

metrics.label: Bank
metrics.description: Use a bank angle appropriate for circling, not exceeding the ACS limit.

criteria: Maintain appropriate circling airspeed and altitude until descent for landing is appropriate.
Remain within the circling area and maintain required visual references.
Apply wind correction and maintain a safe ground track.
Use a bank angle appropriate to conditions and within the ACS limit.
Position the airplane for a normal landing on the selected runway.
Execute a missed approach if visual reference is lost or a safe landing cannot be made.

reviewVariables.label: BANK
reviewVariables.text: Review bank angle and turn radius.

reviewVariables.label: GROUND TRACK
reviewVariables.text: Review runway-relative positioning and wind correction.

reviewVariables.label: VISUAL
reviewVariables.text: Review continuity of required visual references.

reviewVariables.label: MISSED
reviewVariables.text: Review decision-making if the circle became unstable.

source.documentTitle: Instrument Rating – Airplane Airman Certification Standards

landing-from-instrument-approach.name: Landing from an Instrument Approach
landing-from-instrument-approach.objective: Transition from an instrument approach to a safe visual landing.

metrics.label: Transition
metrics.description: Transition from instrument references to visual references without destabilizing the approach.

metrics.label: Landing
metrics.description: Complete a normal landing using appropriate procedures and control inputs.

criteria: Confirm the required visual references before continuing below minimums.
Transition smoothly from instrument to visual references.
Maintain a stabilized flightpath to the landing area.
Use appropriate configuration and wind correction.
Complete a normal landing or go around if the landing cannot be safely completed.

reviewVariables.label: GO-AROUND
reviewVariables.text: Review whether a go-around was warranted.

loss-of-communications.name: Loss of Communications

metrics.label: Procedure
metrics.description: Apply the applicable route, altitude, and clearance-limit procedures.

metrics.label: Navigation
metrics.description: Continue safe aircraft control and navigation while managing the failure.

criteria: Recognize and troubleshoot the communications failure.
Select the appropriate route and altitude under the applicable lost-communications rules.
Use transponder and available communication/navigation resources appropriately.
Maintain aircraft control and situational awareness.
Proceed to the clearance limit and approach as appropriate to the scenario.
Complete appropriate checklist and emergency actions.

reviewVariables.label: RECOGNITION
reviewVariables.text: Review how quickly the failure was recognized.

reviewVariables.label: ROUTE
reviewVariables.text: Review route selection under the scenario.

reviewVariables.label: NAVIGATION
reviewVariables.text: Review position awareness and procedure compliance.

reviewVariables.label: WORKLOAD
reviewVariables.text: Review task prioritization during the failure.

approach-loss-primary-instruments.name: Approach with Loss of Primary Flight Instrument Indicators
approach-loss-primary-instruments.objective: Conduct an instrument approach with simulated loss of primary flight instrument indications.

metrics.label: Control
metrics.description: Maintain positive aircraft control using remaining reliable indications.

metrics.label: Approach
metrics.description: Maintain applicable approach guidance and tolerances using remaining instruments.

criteria: Recognize unreliable or failed primary flight instrument indications.
Use appropriate backup instruments and available systems.
Maintain positive aircraft control and a disciplined instrument cross-check.
Set up and fly the assigned approach using remaining reliable information.
Maintain applicable airspeed, altitude, and guidance tolerances.
Execute a missed approach if the approach becomes unsafe or required information is unavailable.
